key_insight: OA-RAG combines ontology-based formal reasoning with LLM reasoning to improve answer faithfulness and report the strength of supporting evidence.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make medical question-answering systems more transparent, but the abstract does not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical care.
method: Retrieves logical relationships and descriptive annotations from domain ontologies.
Integrates formal reasoning with LLM reasoning through an agent.
Reports ontology evidence and model-assessed grounding: entailed, supported, related, or unrelated.
evidence_signal: Across benchmarks derived from three large-scale ontologies and six real-world medical QA tasks, OA-RAG achieved the best overall performance among evaluated methods, with stronger grounding generally associated with higher accuracy.
watch_item: Grounding levels are model-assessed signals, not guarantees of correctness or clinical reliability.
paper_title: OA-RAG: Ontology-based Agentic RAG for Faithful LLM Reasoning
